name: Shine Bright at Hudson Yards
why: Holiday light installation across the Hudson Yards plaza, running through January 7, 2027.

name: 23rd México Now Festival
why: Four days of panel discussions, film screenings, and musical performances spotlighting contemporary Mexican art and culture, running Tuesday through Friday.

name: Fifth Avenue Snowflake Illumination Ceremony
why: Annual illumination of the iconic holiday snowflake suspended above Fifth Avenue.

name: Brooklyn Eagle Magazine Launch Party
why: Celebration of the Brooklyn Eagle's new print magazine with readings from contributing writers including Dr. Orna Guralnik.

name: Adam Wade: Live in New York
why: 20-time Moth story slam winner Adam Wade performs three to four stories from his catalog with a rotating special guest opening.

name: Loser's Lounge Singalong: Adele + Amy Winehouse
why: Piano bar singalong featuring Adele and Amy Winehouse songs with guest vocalists from Loser's Lounge and pianist Joe McGinty.

name: My Kinda Night! A Queer Variety Show
why: Monthly queer variety night featuring drag, burlesque, sideshow, and more.

name: Winter Lantern Festival: Illuminate the Farm
why: Thousands of handcrafted lanterns light up the historic farm grounds through January 3, 2027.

name: DUMBO Film Festival
venue: DUMBO House + DUMBO Studio + Producers Club
why: 49 independent films from worldwide submissions across Brooklyn and Manhattan venues, through November 23.

name: MIX NYC Queer Experimental Film Festival
why: NYC's longest-running queer film festival presents three nights of experimental films, through November 21.

name: Broadway Under the Stars
why: Free weekly performances and conversations with Broadway stars, continuing Thursdays through December 17 (except Thanksgiving); tonight features excerpts from Operation Mincemeat, The Lost Boys, and Six.

name: You Don't Need a Smartphone with August Lamm
why: Artist and anti-tech activist August Lamm presents her practical guide to downgrading your phone and upgrading your life.

name: SVA MFA Fine Arts Fall 2026 Open Studios
why: 59 MFA art students from around the world open their studios to the public for one evening.

name: Carnegie Hill Concerts: Slowspin
why: Fall season closer blending dream-folk, ambient, and experimental music with sound artist Zeerak Ahmed performing as Slowspin.

name: NYC Magic Ensemble
why: Evening of magicians and mentalists performing at a neighborhood bar.

name: Pancakes + Booze Art Show
why: Pop-up art show with works by over 100 local artists, music, and all-you-can-eat pancakes.

name: You Can Just Build Things [with Hardware] by OpenAI
why: OpenAI-hosted hands-on hardware building event in New York City.

name: Gemini 4 NYC Hackathon with Google DeepMind
why: $20,000 in prizes for teams building with Gemini 4, hosted in collaboration with Google DeepMind.

name: Non-Slop Hackathon (Pangram × Nous Research × Reducto)
why: $3,000 in prizes for builders working to advance non-AI-generated content and tools.

name: The Muppets Take Manhattan
why: Screening of the 1984 film in which Kermit and the Muppets try to bring their college show to Broadway.

name: The Year of Living Dangerously (35mm)
why: 35mm screening of Peter Weir's 1982 political romance set during the 1965 Indonesian coup, starring Mel Gibson and Sigourney Weaver.

name: MoMI After Dark Tour
why: After-hours guided tour of the museum's galleries and exhibitions.

name: MoMI Merch Meet
why: Free artisan market featuring independent makers and designers in the museum lobby.

name: The Muppets Take Manhattan
why: Screening of the 1984 film in which Kermit and the Muppets try to bring their college show to Broadway.

name: Gigi (35mm)
why: 35mm screening of the 1958 Best Picture winner starring Louis Jourdan and Leslie Caron.

name: MoMI After Dark Tour
why: After-hours guided tour of the museum's galleries and exhibitions.

name: GUNPLA Builders Day
why: Free Gundam model-kit (GUNPLA) building event open to enthusiasts of all skill levels.

name: The Minnellis: A Dual Retrospective
why: Dual retrospective tracing the careers of Liza Minnelli and Judy Garland, running through January 24, 2027.

name: Primary Source: Countertenor with Anthony Roth Costanzo
why: Tony Award-winning countertenor Anthony Roth Costanzo discusses his work at the intersection of classical music and contemporary culture.

name: Marilyn Monroe Centennial
why: Major retrospective of photographs and documentation of Marilyn Monroe's life and career by Lawrence Schiller, opening November 20 and running through March 28, 2027.

name: Friday Night Fever!
why: Free after-hours dance party with DJ Kultured Child, celebrating the 'You Should Be Dancing: New York, 1976 and Beyond' exhibition.

name: America in 25 Revolutions Lecture
Lynn Dally on Jimmy Slyde & the Jazz Tap Ensemble
why: Jazz tap pioneer Lynn Dally discusses the legacy of Jimmy Slyde and the Jazz Tap Ensemble, drawing on archival materials from the Jerome Robbins Dance Division.

name: Joanna Jackson Goldman Lectures: Ned Blackhawk on Native Nations & Benjamin Franklin, Part II
why: Part II of historian Ned Blackhawk's lecture exploring Benjamin Franklin's role in Indian affairs conflicts, settler uprisings, and the crisis of Native American diplomacy leading to the Revolution.

name: Screening & Discussion: The Drug in Our Pocket
why: Screening and discussion of a film examining the relationship between smartphones, screen use, youth mental health, and what alternatives might look like.

name: Conversations in Bioethics: Ethics & the Future of Reproduction (IVG)
why: Johns Hopkins bioethicists examine in vitro gametogenesis (IVG), a technology that could expand reproductive options while raising profound ethical questions about the future of human reproduction.

name: Made in New York: The Forces That Shaped a City
why: Professor Rashad Shabazz examines how the Cross Bronx Expressway devastated Black and Puerto Rican communities and how those conditions inadvertently gave rise to hip-hop, using the Library's Robert Moses Papers.

name: Film Screening & Conversation: What Will I Become?
why: Screening of an award-winning documentary exploring trans boyhood, grief, and mental health through the stories of Blake Brockington and Kyler Prescott, followed by a conversation with a co-director, in honor of Trans Day of Remembrance.

name: Adobe Premiere Pro 101: The Basics
why: Free hands-on workshop introducing video editing fundamentals in Premiere Pro: importing, organizing, sequencing, and exporting your own footage.

name: Martha Graham: The Mother of Psychological Dance
why: Large-scale exhibition exploring Martha Graham's work through archival materials, Isamu Noguchi's stage sets, and costumes, extended through January 2, 2027.

name: Silly Old Bear! Winnie-the-Pooh at 100
why: Closing-soon centennial display featuring original mockups, E.H. Shepard illustrations, and the original Pooh stuffed toys; closes November 30.

name: To Uncover and Reveal to the World: Arturo Schomburg's Library
venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
why: Over 100 objects from Arturo Schomburg's original 1926 collection, many on display for the first time; closes December 5.

name: Declaring America: 1776 and Beyond
why: Multi-gallery exhibition unpacking the American Revolution through founding documents, protest ephemera, and artworks from the Library's collections, running through January 10, 2027.

name: Building Tour: P.E. Guerin Architectural Hardware and Foundry
source: AIA New York | Center for Architecture
via: AIA New York | Center for Architecture
why: Guided tour inside P.E. Guerin's historic West Village foundry and showroom, one of the last remaining architectural hardware manufacturers still producing in New York City.

name: Walking Tour: Privately Owned Public Spaces (POPS) in Midtown North
source: AIA New York | Center for Architecture
via: AIA New York | Center for Architecture
why: Expert-led walk through Midtown's legally required privately owned public spaces — plazas, atriums and arcades embedded in towers — examining their design, accessibility, and urban role.

name: AI+A Series, Part 7: From World Models to the Built World
source: AIA New York | Center for Architecture
via: AIA New York | Center for Architecture
why: Half-day workshops and conversations on how AI world models are transforming architectural design practice, from generative tools to spatial reasoning.

name: Reimagining Justice Film Screening: The Alabama Solution
source: AIA New York | Center for Architecture
via: AIA New York | Center for Architecture
why: Documentary screening examining how the design of Alabama's correctional system perpetuates cycles of incarceration, part of AIA's ongoing Reimagining Justice series.

name: Humanist Modernity: Maciej and Stanisława Nowicki
source: AIA New York | Center for Architecture
via: AIA New York | Center for Architecture
why: Exhibition on the visionary Polish-American architect duo whose collaborative postwar work pioneered the integration of modern structure with humanist values, through March 27, 2027.

name: Dark Matter U: Justice, Pedagogy, Design
source: AIA New York | Center for Architecture
via: AIA New York | Center for Architecture
why: Exhibition exploring how architecture schools at HBCUs and other institutions have shaped a tradition of racially inclusive design pedagogy and social justice practice, through March 27, 2027.

name: Why Design?
source: AIA New York | Center for Architecture
via: AIA New York | Center for Architecture
why: Gallery exhibition posing fundamental questions about design's purpose, process, and responsibility through artifacts, drawings, and projects; closes January 2, 2027.

name: David Reinfurt for Open Flat File
venue: Frederick P. Rose Auditorium, 41 Cooper Square
why: Designer David Reinfurt presents a lecture on a 1986 Visible Language article about TOKENS as part of the Herb Lubalin Center's Open Flat File series; each lecturer responds to a single archival object and distributes a free commemorative poster at the event.

name: MAS Walking Tour: Grand Central Terminal
source: Municipal Art Society of New York
via: Municipal Art Society of New York
why: MAS docent-led tour inside Grand Central Terminal exploring its architecture, engineering, and history, offered on multiple dates through the month.

name: MAS Walking Tour: Ready for Occupancy — Early Apartment Houses in Greenwich Village
source: Municipal Art Society of New York
via: Municipal Art Society of New York
why: Expert-led walking tour with Matt Postal tracing the architectural evolution of early apartment buildings in Greenwich Village, from first tenements to luxury flats.

name: MAS Walking Tour: 400 Years of Flatbush
source: Municipal Art Society of New York
via: Municipal Art Society of New York
why: Walking tour with Zack Rhodes through one of Brooklyn's oldest neighborhoods, covering four centuries of Dutch colonial settlement, Caribbean immigration, and urban change.

name: AIRWAY | Stories from the ER
why: Eight emergency physicians from Maimonides and other NYC hospitals take the stage at CBH to share firsthand ER stories in AIRWAY, the storytelling series founded by Dr. Mert Erogul, Dr. Josh Schiller, and Dr. Arlene Chung — described as The Moth meets The Pitt.

name: Black Empowerment and a Brooklyn Fabric Company: The Story of Bed-Stuy Restoration's Design Works
why: Panel discussion on Design Works, a 1969 Black-run textile studio in Bedford-Stuyvesant that created jobs, celebrated African heritage through bold fabrics, and sought to revitalize Bed-Stuy through economic empowerment and community control.

name: The Battle of Brooklyn
why: Free in-depth guided tours of the exhibition marking the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, exploring the pivotal 1776 battle fought in Brooklyn through rare artifacts, maps, and primary sources from the CBH collection.

name: 12th Annual Fort Greene Holiday Tree Lighting
venue: Fort Greene Park (NW corner, Myrtle Ave & St. Edward's St entrance)
why: Annual neighborhood tree lighting ceremony with live holiday music from Brooklyn Music School, free hot cocoa, and a Myrtle Avenue Toy Drive for NYCHA families.

name: Fort Greene Artisans Bazaar
venue: DeKalb Ave between S. Oxford St and Washington Park
why: 30+ local designers, artisans, and makers along DeKalb Avenue at Fort Greene Park every Saturday, with up-cycled fashion, handmade jewelry, small-batch apothecary, granola, and more.

name: Leaf No Trace
venue: Fort Greene Park (meet at Visitors Center)
why: Annual community leaf raking day in Fort Greene Park; collected leaves are stored in a corral and left to become nutrient-rich leaf mould for the park's trees.

name: Birding: Winter Birds with Urban Park Rangers
venue: Fort Greene Park (meet at Visitors Center)
why: Ranger-led walk through Fort Greene Park identifying winter resident birds and migratory visitors; no registration required.

name: King's County Fitness Club
why: Free community-led outdoor workout at the Fort Greene Park Monument Plaza every Wednesday morning, welcoming all ages and abilities, with coffee afterward.

name: NYTM Holiday Train Show at Grand Central
why: 22nd annual holiday train show: Lionel trains including vintage subway sets and the Polar Express circle a 34-foot two-level layout passing NYC landmarks, now featuring new buildings by artist Danny Cortes and a miniature Economy Candy.

name: Holiday Nostalgia Train Rides
why: Vintage subway cars from the Transit Museum's collection run on the F and Q lines every Sunday from Thanksgiving to New Year's, offering free rides aboard restored mid-20th century trains.

name: Transit Walk: Downtown Brooklyn
why: Expert-led walking tour tracing Downtown Brooklyn's transformation over 400 years through ferry landings, former trolley routes, elevated train ghosts, and the subway era, ending at the Transit Museum's historic Court Street Station.

name: Transit Walk: Second Avenue's Art and Transit History
venue: East Side Manhattan (meet point on registration)
neighborhood: Upper East Side / Midtown East, Manhattan
why: Walking tour along Second Avenue exploring a century of transit development and the Q line's public art collection by Jean Shin, Vik Muniz, and Sarah Sze, with a stop at a surviving original trolley kiosk on the Queensboro Bridge.

name: Transit Walk: Deep Dive — Grand Central's Tracks and Trains
time: 11:00 AM (also 2:00 PM; dates in January too)
why: In-depth tour of Grand Central's ever-evolving rail infrastructure, from its original electrified tunnels through the new Grand Central Madison expansion.

name: Transit Walk: Art and Design Secrets of Penn Station and Moynihan Train Hall
time: 11:00 AM (also 2:00 PM; dates in January too)
why: Expert-led tour uncovering the Beaux-Arts remnants of the original Penn Station and the new public artworks of Moynihan Train Hall, from hidden architectural details to contemporary commissions.

name: MTA Open Data for System Improvements
why: MTA data scientists and operations directors explain how the agency uses Open Data to bundle maintenance work orders, reduce service disruptions, and communicate closures to riders.

name: Transit Trivia
why: Annual transit knowledge showdown at Pig Beach BBQ in Astoria — teams of two to six compete on subway, rail, and transit history. Must be 21+; sells out in advance.

name: MCNY Holiday Market
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: Annual holiday artisan market with Brooklyn Pop-Up vendors inside MCNY, free to browse without museum admission.

name: MCNY Holiday Market
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: Annual holiday artisan market with Brooklyn Pop-Up vendors inside MCNY, free to browse without museum admission.

name: NYBG Holiday Train Show: 35th Anniversary
why: 35th anniversary of the beloved Haupt Conservatory train show, featuring G-scale model trains winding through over 175 NYC landmark replicas handcrafted from plant materials; runs through January 18, 2027.

name: BBG Lightscape
time: Evening hours (see website for times and dates)
why: Annual illuminated trail through BBG reimagined each year with new artist installations: this season features Moon and Stars, a 30-foot floating inflatable sphere by Culture Creative; Winter Wonder lighting Cherry Esplanade by ITHACA Studio; and Wisps near Magnolia Plaza by Pitaya. Opens Nov 20.

name: Central Park Conservancy 30th Annual Holiday Lighting Ceremony
time: Evening (date TBD — RSVP for exact time)
why: 30th anniversary of Central Park's holiday tree flotilla lighting on the Harlem Meer, with carol singing, hot cocoa, and the annual spectacle of illuminated trees reflected in the water.

name: Skating Programs at the Gottesman Rink
venue: Wollman Rink / Davis Center, Central Park
why: 2026–27 winter ice skating season is open at the Gottesman Rink, with Learn to Skate, Community Skate, hockey, and figure skating programs for beginners through experienced skaters.

name: Make a Holiday Wreath
why: Hands-on workshop to design and assemble a custom holiday wreath at Brooklyn Craft Co.'s Greenpoint studio; all materials provided.

name: Bookbinding 101: DIY Journals
why: Intro bookbinding class making your own hand-bound journal with a sewn signature binding — a practical craft skill and a thoughtful handmade gift.

name: Knitting 102: Chunky Sweater
why: Multi-session knitting workshop for those who know the basics; you'll knit a full chunky sweater in bulky yarn using simple construction techniques.

name: Flat Felting: Floral Bouquet
why: Flat felting workshop using wool roving and barbed needles to create a colorful floral bouquet — a satisfying tactile craft with no sewing required.

name: Make a Custom Snow Globe
why: Build a custom personalized snow globe from scratch with your own miniature scene inside — an unusual hands-on craft and a satisfying holiday keepsake to keep or give.

name: Needle Felted Pets
why: Needle felting workshop to sculpt a miniature 3D portrait of your pet (or a friend's) in wool — instructors provide reference photos guidance and all tools.

name: 50 Years of Free Expression with Franklin Furnace
why: Franklin Furnace founder Martha Wilson celebrates the 50th anniversary of the organization — which supported Jenny Holzer, Ana Mendieta, Karen Finley and hundreds more during the culture wars — with readings, Martha Wilson trivia with prizes, and cake.

name: Tellus Audio Cassette Magazine Anthology Vol. 1 — Listening Session & Conversation
why: Listening session for the newly compiled first volume of Tellus Audio Cassette Magazine, the influential 1983–1996 NYC cassette art series that distributed experimental sound works by Laurie Anderson, John Cage, and others via mail.

name: Our Gay Children: NYC Gay Liberation Marches, 1979–80
why: Presentation and signing for a photographic archive of New York City Gay Liberation marches from 1979–80, documenting the early movement through candid street photography from the Christopher Street parades.

name: A Conversation with Tyne Rafaeli and Laurie Anderson
why: Laurie Anderson and director Tyne Rafaeli discuss the upcoming Broadway revival of Clifford Odets' Awake and Sing! — a Depression-era Bronx immigrant family drama — and the resonance of immigrant stories with today's debates about dignity and survival.

name: An Evening of Storytelling: Writers on Family History
why: Ava Chin, Jelani Cobb, Ada Ferrer, Vivian Gornick, and others read from their work and discuss family history inside the Tenement Museum's recreated apartments on Orchard Street, followed by a reception and book signing in the Visitor Center.

name: Going Behind the Scenes with The Gilded Age
why: Emmy-winning Production Designer Bob Shaw and Emmy-nominated Costume Designer Kasia Walicka Maimone discuss how they created the visual world of HBO's The Gilded Age Season 3, including research visits to the Tenement Museum to authenticate the LES tenement sequences.

name: The Sugar Plum Ball: Fabulous Winter Waacking Battle
venue: Museum of the City of New York, 1220 Fifth Ave
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: Competitive Waacking battle at MCNY — a street dance form born in 1970s LGBTQ underground clubs, here set to Tchaikovsky with Princess Lockerooo hosting, theatrical costume contest included, as part of the Winter Waacking Festival.

name: Prospect Park NYE: 46th Annual New Year's Eve Fireworks
why: 46th annual fireworks celebration in Prospect Park, Brooklyn's largest park, with live entertainment beginning at 10pm and a fireworks display at midnight over the Long Meadow.

name: Ice Skating at Prospect Park Lakeside
venue: LeFrak Center at Lakeside, Prospect Park
why: 2026–27 ice skating season is open at Prospect Park's Lakeside complex, with covered and open-air rinks plus figure skating and ice hockey classes and leagues.

name: The Oyster by Alan Michelson — Public Art Installation
time: Open during ferry hours; on view through November 30
price: Free with ferry ($5 roundtrip, free for many)
why: Monumental site-responsive sculpture by Mohawk artist Alan Michelson — grounded in Lenape oyster middens and pre-colonial shell rings — acts simultaneously as habitat, monument, and gathering place, addressing erasure of indigenous lifeways in the harbor. Closing November 30.

name: Holiday Card Workshop with Evan Bellantone
venue: Lower East Side Printshop, 306 W. 37th Street 6th Fl.
price: $175 (includes all materials and 7 hours of studio time)
why: Full-day printmaking workshop for creating an edition of handmade holiday cards using relief printing, collage, and embossing techniques; participants are encouraged to bring their own materials (magazine cutouts, textured paper, watercolors) for a playful, experimental session.

name: Engineering for Humanity with Gerald Chan
venue: Columbia University, Davis Auditorium, 530 W 120th St
why: Gerald Chan, founder of Morningside Group and philanthropist behind major Columbia University and Harvard engineering programs, speaks on the intersection of engineering, science, and human flourishing.

name: Dev AI NYC: Jane Pek & Chenda Ngak
why: Jane Pek, author of AI fiction novels The Verifiers and The Rivals, reads and discusses the craft of writing about AI — alongside Chenda Ngak (Head of Comms, Automattic) — at the company whose platform powers much of the web's editorial writing.

name: Statistics in the Era of Computation — Kyunghyun Cho
venue: Simons Foundation, 160 5th Ave, Gerald D. Fischbach Auditorium
why: NYU Professor Kyunghyun Cho — a pioneer in neural machine translation and sequence modeling — speaks on how modern computational methods are reshaping statistical inference, at the Simons Foundation's public lecture series.

name: Distribution Is Your Moat — Rachel Schindler
why: Rachel Schindler, founder of Punchbowl News (the Capitol Hill news outlet that broke numerous congressional scoops), speaks on how distribution strategy — not content alone — determines who survives in modern media.

name: Behind The Brands: Marc Lore
why: Marc Lore — founder of Diapers.com (sold to Amazon for $545M), Jet.com (sold to Walmart for $3.3B), and current CEO of Wonder — speaks on building consumer brands and the future of food delivery at this NYU Stern public series.

name: The Gorgeous Nothings: LGBTQ+ History Tour & Talk, Roosevelt Island
why: Walking tour, panel discussion, and singalong on Roosevelt Island exploring the secret wing of the men's penitentiary where queer culture flourished in the 1930s — the setting of new musical The Gorgeous Nothings by Life Jacket Theater.

name: Before New York with Eric W. Sanderson
why: Eric Sanderson (NYBotanic Garden), author of the bestselling Mannahatta, presents Before New York — using centuries of ecological maps and research to show the five boroughs as they looked 400 years ago, including what has vanished from the landscape and what might be restored.

name: New City Critics: Place Perspectives — Lower East Side
why: 2026 New City Critics fellows — a diverse cohort of emerging architecture and urban design critics — share their written pieces about places in transition, presented with Urban Design Forum and the Architectural League of New York.
